Economy & Markets
• Big Tech led a global rout as investors balked at soaring AI capex and weak results; Alphabet warned AI search summaries hurt ads, while Amazon and Intel missed expectations and signaled cash burn.
• Binance disclosed a record $6.3bn crypto heist and paused withdrawals, rattling digital assets already under pressure.
• Oil majors reported windfall profits from higher refining margins and tight supplies, with BP’s earnings hitting an 18-year high and ExxonMobil/Chevron warning on diesel.
• Macro currents: France’s economy contracted 0.1% in Q3; the euro headed for its worst month vs the pound since 2022; UK debt managers tilted issuance to shorter gilts; ECB tightened scrutiny of complex risk transfers.
• Corporate moves and policy: Microsoft plans a $25bn debt raise to fund AI; AWS pledged heavy spend to chase $1T revenue; GM pays $220m in a data-privacy settlement; Trump flagged foreign robot imports as a security threat; Utah brought felony charges against prediction market Kalshi.
Why it matters: Markets are recalibrating the true cost and timeline of the AI buildout amid cyber, energy, and macro shocks that challenge earnings, liquidity, and policy.

• Analysis highlighted North Korea’s ascent as a hacking power amid sanctions and cash needs.
Why it matters: Shifting battlelines, deeper defense industrial ties, and escalating cyber exposure are reshaping security dynamics across Europe and the Indo-Pacific.

• Biomed and imaging: First-in-human CRISPR prime editing trial began for Wilson disease; ultra-fast 3D microscopy captures living cells; studies probed enzyme dynamics in crowded droplets and quantum states in multilayer graphene.
• Life and environment: Antarctic penguin deaths were traced to cholera, not avian flu; fruit/vegetable skins pack more fiber; plant-inspired PFAS alternatives advanced; birds can suffer jet lag and veer off course.
• Chips and data: HBM shortages threaten AI expansion; an open-source tool lets Withings users sync health data without subscriptions.
Why it matters: Platform upgrades, space capabilities, and biomedical breakthroughs are converging with materials science and data access to redefine innovation cycles.

Entertainment.title: My Chemical Romance and Lauren Tsai Merge Worlds in ‘Prelude to The End’
Entertainment.text: SummaryMy Chemical Romance and Lauren Tsai launch the animated short Prelude to The End.The film merges The Black Parade with Tsai’s The Dying World.Billie Eilish, Phoebe Bridgers and Hideo Kojima contribute voices.My Chemical Romance have entered Lauren Tsai’s The Dying World with Prelude to The End, a new animated short film that folds the visual artist’s surreal universe into the mythology surrounding The Black Parade.Produced by Tsai’s independent studio UNREAL INC., the film follows Astrid through an uncanny New England boarding school slowly disappearing beneath mountains of discarded objects and trash. After school authorities confiscate and throw away her cherished sketchbook, Astrid follows it down a garbage chute and tumbles into a strange subterranean realm populated by abandoned ideas, including one of her own that has continued to haunt her. The hand-drawn journey moves between oppressive school corridors and increasingly dreamlike imagery, using Astrid’s confrontation with creativity, conformity and forgotten parts of herself to echo the themes of identity and self-expression that have long run through My Chemical Romance’s work. Tsai voices Astrid, while Billie Eilish appears as her friend, Phoebe Bridgers as her sister, Hideo Kojima as The Teacher and John C. McGinley as the imposing Dean.The collaboration arrives alongside the 20th-anniversary edition of The Black Parade, with the short incorporating “The End,” the 2006 album’s opening track, into Tsai’s existing narrative world. The Dying World first appeared as a short film at the 2025 Annecy International Animation Film Festival before expanding through Tsai’s large-scale installation at Hollywood Forever Cemetery later that year, making the MCR crossover a particularly personal one for an artist who has cited the band as a formative influence and created animated fan videos for its music as a child.Read more at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Little Napoli’s New Menu Goes Deeper Into Neapolitan Comfort Food
Entertainment.text: SummaryLittle Napoli expanded its Wan Chai menu with new antipasti, pastas, and desserts.Chef Gavino Pilo introduced an extra-large 40cm "Cart Wheel" style Neapolitan pizza.The MICHELIN-awarded pizzeria maintains its signature 90-second stone-oven baking process.Little Napoli is stretching beyond the pizza oven with its most extensive menu expansion since opening in Hong Kong in 2021, giving Chef and Owner Gavino Pilo more room to explore the food culture of his native Naples. Available this fall at the restaurant’s Wan Chai location, the new offering introduces four antipasti, seven hot plates and fresh pastas, five desserts and eight Special Creation pizzas, while expanding the overall pizza selection to 27 varieties.Recognized with a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand 2026 and a Top 30 spot in 50 Top Pizza Asia-Pacific 2026, the restaurant is broadening its focus beyond its established roots as a neighborhood takeaway. The refreshed culinary direction introduces four new antipasti, seven hot plates and fresh pastas, five desserts and a collection of Special Creation pizzas, bringing the total pizza selection to 27.Guests can now start their dining experience with elevated appetizers like Carpaccio di Polpo featuring Mediterranean octopus and Amalfi lemon zest, or dive into comforting hot plates such as the crispy Crochetta di Patate Ripiena and Ziti alla Genovese with slow-braised beef. Pasta now receives greater prominence too, spanning homemade Gnocchi alla Sorrentina, slow-braised beef Ziti alla Genovese, pork-and-beef Cavatelli al Ragù Napoletano, and a lighter fettuccine topped with Sicilian shrimp tartare, heirloom tomatoes and Amalfi lemon.Pizza nevertheless remains Little Napoli’s anchor, with Pilo using the expanded format to move between tradition and more expressive combinations. New Special Creations include the Luciana, topped with Mediterranean octopus, San Marzano tomato, Gaeta olives, garlic and chilli; the Parigina, built around a buffalo ricotta-stuffed crust, smoked ham and smoked Agerola mozzarella; and the sweet-and-savory Cilentana, combining Capocollo, buffalo blue cheese and Cilento fig sauce.The restaurant has also introduced old-school 40cm Pizza a Ruota di Carro, or “Cart Wheel” pizzas, characterized by their oversized diameter and exceptionally thin crust spilling over the plate. Alongside the new arrivals, Little Napoli continues to be defined by the classic Neapolitan pizzas that established its following, including Marinara, Margherita, Diavola and Vesuviana, all made from fresh daily dough and baked to order in a traditional stone oven. Its Pizza Fritta remains another deeply Neapolitan staple, while the expanded dessert section adds Ricottamisù, Rum Babbà and Mini Sfogliatella Riccia — rounding out a menu that gives diners a broader taste of Naples without losing sight of the pizzas at its core.LIttle Napoli6-16 Tai Wong St E, Wan Chai,Hong Kong Island, Hong Kong  View this post on Instagram  Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Donald Glover Drops Into Netflix’s Live-Action ‘PUBG’ Series
Entertainment.text: SummaryNetflix is developing a live-action series based on the battle royale hit 'PlayerUnknown’s Battlegrounds'Donald Glover is set to star, write, executive produce and direct, with brother Stephen Glover co-writing and executive producingThe creative team faces an unusual challenge, since the game itself has no storyline to adaptNetflix is developing a live-action PUBG series with Donald Glover attached to lead. Based on Krafton’s 2017 battle royale PlayerUnknown’s Battlegrounds, the project would put Glover in charge both in front of the camera and behind it, with the multihyphenate also writing, executive producing and planning to direct.The creative core of the series is a familiar one. Donald will write and executive produce alongside his brother Stephen Glover, reuniting a duo whose partnership defined FX’s Atlanta, which Donald created and starred in while Stephen wrote and executive produced across all four seasons. The pair has since collaborated on Amazon’s Swarm and the musical film Guava Island, and Stephen also wrote for Donald’s Mr. and Mrs. Smith series at Amazon.The producing lineup brings together film, management and gaming expertise. Michael Schaefer is executive producing for Neon TV, Fam Udeorji is on board for Gilga, and Taeseok Jang and Sujin Lee represent LV3H, the entertainment division of Krafton. That last involvement means the studio behind the game will have a direct hand in how it translates to the screen.The biggest open question is what the show will actually be about. PUBG has no narrative to speak of. Each match drops a large group of players onto one of several maps stocked with weapons, vehicles and gear, and the last player standing wins. Without a built-in story, characters or lore to follow, the writers are working with a premise rather than a plot, and specific story details for the series remain under wraps.The source material’s reach is not in question. Nearly a decade after release, PUBG remains one of the most-played games in the world, drawing hundreds of thousands of daily active players after setting multiple Guinness World Records at launch.The project would also add to Netflix’s growing slate of game adaptations. The streamer is developing an Assassin’s Creed series and a live-action Gears of War film, along with animated takes on Clash of Clans and Minecraft, and it already streams Splinter Cell: Deathwatch and Cyberpunk: Edgerunners.Stay tuned for more info.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: A24’s ‘You Can See Everything’ Popcorn Bucket Takes Transparency Literally
Entertainment.text: SummaryA24 has unveiled a fully see-through popcorn bucket tied to 'You Can See Everything,' Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s documentary on Theranos founder Elizabeth HolmesThe design leans into the film’s title, putting every kernel on display through a clear shellThe bucket lands as the documentary posts box office numbers rarely seen for nonfiction filmA24 is marking the release of You Can See Everything with the You Can See Everything Popcorn Bucket, a fully transparent tub that turns the film’s title into a design brief. Billed by A24 with the tagline “Radical Transparency,” the bucket swaps the usual printed cardboard for a clear shell that leaves nothing hidden, a fitting gesture for a documentary built on total access to one of Silicon Valley’s most infamous founders.The silhouette borrows from the classic movie theater popcorn box, tapering from a wide mouth down to a narrower base. A wavy, scalloped rim gives the top edge a playful finish, the one decorative flourish on an otherwise stripped-back piece. Because the walls are completely clear, the popcorn itself becomes the main visual, and the bucket only looks finished once it’s filled.Branding is kept deliberately sparse. The film’s title is printed in bold black sans-serif type across two staggered lines near the middle of the bucket, appearing to hover over the popcorn behind it, while a small A24 logo sits toward the bottom.The concept makes more sense once you know the film. Directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, You Can See Everything opens 34 days before Elizabeth Holmes, the Theranos founder convicted of defrauding investors, reports to prison, when she invites a film crew to document her life. Holmes hadn’t sat for an interview in a decade, yet she let Fielder and his crew into the San Diego home she shares with partner Billy Evans, the father of her two children, on the premise that they could see everything. The project stretches well beyond that window, with the film’s second half following the crew as it reworks its approach after Holmes enters prison and access to her becomes limited. A clear bucket and a “Radical Transparency” tagline read as a wink at that premise, and at a subject whose company collapsed over what it kept hidden.The film has also become a genuine commercial outlier. It opened to $15 million USD from 855 screens, the second-best opening ever for a non-music documentary behind Fahrenheit 9/11, with A24 reporting more than 2,000 sellouts. Rather than dropping off, ticket sales grew in its second weekend, bringing in $19.5 million USD from 2,655 theaters. The documentary has reportedly crossed $50 million USD domestically, making it only the third non-music documentary to do so after March of the Penguins and Fahrenheit 9/11. Trade coverage has framed the run as a break from the slump documentaries have faced at the box office over the past five years, alongside talk that it could become the first documentary nominated for Best Picture. A24 kept the film’s twists under wraps through release, and a ticket-gated bucket fits that event-style rollout.The bucket can’t be bought on its own. It is reserved for fans who purchase a ticket to You Can See Everything after 1 p.m. EST on October 28, and claiming it requires logging in with the same email used for the ticket order. Each order is capped at one bucket, and stock is limited.Eligible ticket holders can add the You Can See Everything Popcorn Bucket to their cart via the A24 Shop now, with orders shipping by November 20.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: The McDonald’s ‘Pokémon’ Happy Meal Is Back This November With 15 Toys and Trading Cards
Entertainment.text: SummaryMcDonald’s has confirmed the return of its 'Pokémon' Happy Meal with a 15-piece toy set and a 15-card trading card collectionPikachu, Eevee, Charmander, Squirtle and Umbreon headline the lineup, with leaked cards pointing to deeper cuts like Metagross, Zoroark and JirachiThe promotion launches in the US first before rolling out across Europe, Asia, Latin America and beyond over the following monthsThe McDonald’s Pokémon Happy Meal is officially making a comeback, with the fast food giant confirming a US launch on November 10. The latest edition gives collectors two sets to chase, pairing 15 collectible toys with 15 collectible trading cards, alongside a digital game built into the packaging itself.The toys take the shape of miniature Happy Meal boxes, each one carrying the face of a different Pokémon, and they’re designed to do more than sit on a shelf. McDonald’s executive Guillaume Huin offered a closer look at the figures, showing that each box-shaped toy converts into a bag charm. McDonald’s has confirmed Pikachu, Eevee, Charmander, Squirtle and Umbreon as part of the roster, while promotional artwork shows Piplup and Eevee emerging from Happy Meal boxes with Pikachu front and center on the packaging.Huin also gave fans an early glimpse at the trading cards, which make up the second half of the drop. His preview featured Jirachi, Pikachu and Absol among several other fan favorites, though McDonald’s has not detailed the complete 15-card checklist.The box itself doubles as a gateway to a digital side quest. Entertainment.text: SummaryKobe Bryant's game-worn Lower Merion High School uniform has sold for $2.2 million USD at Sotheby'sThe final result sets a new world record for a high school basketball jersey eclipsing the $1.3 million USD mark set by LeBron JamesThe uniform drew 26 bids from seven collectors after previously selling for $51,400 USD in 2013Sotheby’s has officially sold Kobe Bryant’s game-worn Lower Merion High School uniform for a historic $2.2 million USD, establishing a new world record for any high school basketball jersey sold at auction. The landmark sale concluded on October 28 following an intense bidding battle that pushed the piece far past its initial presale estimate.The auction accumulated 26 bids across seven competing bidders, propelling the final hammer price past the initial estimate in excess of $1 million USD. At $2.2 million USD, the sale breaks the previous record for a high-school basketball jersey, which was established in 2024 when LeBron James’ St. Vincent-St. Mary jersey from his famous 2002 Sports Illustrated "The Chosen One" cover sold for $1.3 million USD. The sale highlights the meteoric expansion of the sports collectibles landscape, with this exact Kobe uniform previously commanding $51,400 USD when it last sold in 2013.The uniform is matched specifically to Kobe’s junior season during a March 1995 matchup against Hazleton Area, representing a crucial developmental stage one year before he led Lower Merion to the Pennsylvania state championship. Highlighting the cultural weight of the artifact, Brahm Wachter, Sotheby’s Head of Modern Collectables, shared: “This Lower Merion jersey is where Kobe's story starts, before the rings, the records, and the Mamba Mentality, when he was just a kid in a gym outworking everyone. Art & Culture.title: REdDUO’s STEM VASE Is Built for Just One Flower
Art & Culture.text: SummaryRedDuo’s STEM VASE reduces the traditional vase to a sculptural steel framework for one flower.Two staggered prisms support a tilted disc with a single stem opening.Two sizes are offered; prices start at €720 EUR ( approx. $806 USD).REdDUO strips the vase back until almost nothing remains but the flower itself. Its new STEM VASE is conceived as an architectural framework for displaying a single stem, replacing the familiar enclosed vessel with a precise composition of steel planes and volumes. Two staggered prismatic forms rise vertically to support a tilted disc punctured by one small opening, through which the flower emerges. The arrangement gives the object a distinctly structural quality, somewhere between miniature architecture and functional sculpture, while intentionally leaving the organic form of the plant as the visual focal point.Made entirely from steel and left in a steel finish, STEM VASE avoids decorative embellishment in favor of sharp geometry, exposed material and carefully balanced proportions. The angled upper disc introduces tension against the upright base, while the offset volumes prevent the silhouette from becoming overly rigid or symmetrical.The construction makes the mechanics of the object immediately legible: every element appears to have a clear role in supporting and positioning the stem. REdDUO describes the design as one in which “structure and function are one,” an idea that gives the industrial-looking object its visual clarity while creating a deliberate contrast with the softness and irregularity of a flower.STEM VASE is offered in two proportions, allowing the same architectural idea to shift in scale without changing its underlying language. The taller STEM VASE 01 measures 471 mm high by 120 mm wide and is priced at €795 EUR (approx. $890 USD), while the more compact STEM VASE 02 stands 337 mm high by 86 mm wide and is priced at €720 EUR ( approx. $806 USD). Art & Culture.text: SummaryNorman Foster partners with Lebond on his first-ever watch design.The 38.5mm titanium model features an integrated strap and 12-hour bezel for dual-time tracking.Natural titanium and black DLC editions each use an ETA 2892-A2 automatic caliber.Norman Foster is bringing his design language to watchmaking for the first time, partnering with independent brand Lebond on a pair of mechanical watches shaped by the same ideas of proportion, engineering and functional clarity that define his architectural work.Developed alongside the Norman Foster Foundation’s Design & Innovation Unit, the project treats the watch as an everyday tool rather than a miniature architectural statement, with Foster drawing on his experience as a pilot and frequent traveler. That influence is most apparent in the bidirectional 12-hour bezel, which allows a second time zone to be tracked without adding a conventional GMT hand, while the case eliminates traditional lugs entirely so the integrated rubber strap flows directly from the watch and wraps closely around the wrist.The watch arrives in two interpretations built around the same 38.5mm Grade 5 titanium case, measuring just 10mm thick and offering 50 meters of water resistance. The Natural Titanium Edition combines matte sandblasted, brushed and polished surfaces with a sunray-finished dial, polished nickel hands and a light grey FKM rubber strap, while the Black Edition takes a more instrument-like approach with matte black DLC-coated titanium, a black lacquered dial and matching strap.Both feature blue-emitting Super-LumiNova, a date window at 3 o’clock and interchangeable integrated straps with titanium deployant clasps. Through the sapphire caseback, an ETA 2892-A2 automatic caliber provides 50 hours of power reserve, distinguished by a custom five-perforation rotor rendered in vivid blue on the natural titanium version and red on the black model.Rather than treating the collaboration as a one-off exercise in styling, Foster designed the watch around adaptability, with the modular strap attachment intended to let owners personalize the piece as additional combinations are introduced over time. The restrained typography, compact proportions and visible movement all reinforce his stated preference for an object that feels “timeless rather than fashionable,” while the integrated construction gives the watch a distinctly architectural sense of continuity. Both the Lebond Norman Foster Natural Titanium Edition and Black Edition are available to order now through Lebond, priced at €3,500 EUR each (approx. $4,000 USD).Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Artificial Intelligence.title: Consumer Appetite for Personal AI Goes Mainstream
Artificial Intelligence.text: This article is brought to you by Qualcomm Technologies.For many consumers, much of the promise and appeal of AI is personal. Consumers are looking past generic tools and want to know how these technologies will help them in their daily lives. These trends coincide with the advent of new classes of wearable devices that, in addition to being able to leverage powerful frontier models, feature built-in intelligence that understand the context of a user. Where are they? What are they seeing and hearing? What are their habits, their preferences, their schedules?It’s an astonishing pivot, from passive accessories that served mostly to send users smartphone notifications to proactive, intelligent companions. The smartphone is no longer the center of that universe; though it’s still incredibly important, in this personal AI paradigm, the AI is the UI. And it shifts the focus toward you, the user.These new technologies are exciting. But what do consumers really want?A Personal AI report, commissioned by Qualcomm Technologies, built on a survey of more than 12,000 people across key geographies worldwide (the U.S., U.K., Germany, India, Brazil, and China) focused on the rise of personal AI in intelligent wearables looks deeply at these developments.The smartphone is no longer the center of that universe; though it’s still incredibly important, in this personal AI paradigm, the AI is the UI.Survey respondents are less interested in single devices and are responding more to the idea of connected ecosystems. As people expand their roster of devices, it only makes sense. Instead of relying entirely on a smartphone and a laptop, respondents also have connected technology in their cars, as well as intelligent wearables like smartwatches, smart glasses, hearables, and other wearables like rings, pins, and pendants. They want those devices to work in concert, and the way to do that is to decentralize any single one of them. Instead, the AI agent that knows the user and works across all of those devices becomes the unifying factor.Consider a typical workday: A user’s watch detects it is time to leave for a meeting and, with permission, their AI agent factors in calendar details, real-time traffic and battery status across their devices. In the car, it suggests the best route and briefs them on their meeting agenda. As they arrive, smart glasses surface a discreet reminder, such as the meeting location or the name of a new contact, while the phone stays in their pocket. No one device has to do everything; each plays the role it is best suited for, coordinated by a personal AI agent that understands the user’s context and acts only at the user’s direction.With this in mind, simply adding more hardware to the mix isn’t sufficient. Even though respondents will be open to new form factors, they’ll demand more from their ecosystem of devices. They’ll be sensitive to points of friction and needless complexity, and they’ll require each new device to bring something new to the table — “incremental intelligence, convenience, or contextual awareness that their existing devices cannot deliver on their own what the report,” reads the report.The usage trends are up. The report found that those who own wearables are already using AI frequently (60 percent use it at least weekly), which indicates that it’s becoming less of a fun experiment for early adopters and more of a critical mass habit.The “always-on” nature of intelligent wearables appears to be winning respondents, too. The report found the following statistics on average continuous wear among users:True wireless earbuds – 3 hoursWireless headphones – 3 hoursSmart glasses – 5 hoursAudio glasses – 6 hoursSmartwatches – 9 hoursSmart rings, necklaces and pendants – 8 hoursConsumers want AI that is personal and understands their context — they’re looking for smooth, intuitive experiences that are marked by privacy, security, and user control.Consumer Trust Is Hard-WonBut for all the excitement and engagement around intelligent wearables, there’s a gating factor: trust. As use cases for intelligent wearables expands to more personal and persistent experiences, trust is a necessity for Personal AI.The top reported issues around adoption are privacy, security, and user control. The data points to a certain amount of caution around deeply personal use cases, like voice, health, and location, as almost 60 percent of respondents want to keep data from their wearables private, or at least insist on gaining approval before it gets shared.In other words, even though premium features like high-quality audio, perception sensing, battery life, and comfort whet consumer appetites (and agentic AI capabilities drive upgrade intent), true adoption will come only with consumer trust. They want security, privacy, transparency and control.Notably, the report found that respondents expressed more interest in adopting intelligent wearables when Snapdragon was introduced as the enabling platform. This reinforces the value of having an established, trusted technology foundation in the mix.The Industry Remains FluidThe report shows that consumer appetite for AI is high, with 60-70 percent of those surveyed expressing interest in advanced AI as they consider a new device. That’s a constant. But remaining purchase drivers differed between device categories.Audio playback quality is the most influential purchase driver for true wireless earbuds and headphones. For smartwatches, it’s display quality and responsiveness. Respondents are less concerned about technical specifications than aesthetics like materials and finish when it comes to devices like smart rings and pendants. And for smart glasses, it’s all about the type of control, whether it’s voice, gesture, or touch. aspect_ratioThe Rise of Personal AI in Intelligent WearablesArtificial intelligence is entering a new phase, one that is deeply personal, continuously present, and seamlessly embedded into the devices we wear every day. This evolution, which we define as “Personal AI”, represents a shift away from generic, cloud-only intelligence toward AI that understands individuals in context: their habits, preferences, environments, and intent, in real time.Get the full report → Alongside these purchase drivers is another key finding: Consumer appetite for Personal AI agents has gone mainstream. The report says that 70 percent of respondents “express strong interest in an AI assistant that can interact naturally through voice and seamlessly manage devices, apps, and everyday tasks.” With each individual as the center of their own ecosystem, voice becomes the most critical, natural method for interacting with agents.The OpportunityThe industry for intelligent wearables is exciting. It’s clear that consumer demand for Personal AI is high, and this report dives deeply into the specifics of what respondents want out of it. They want AI that is personal and understands their context, and they want it to be proactive and helpful instead of merely reactive. They’re looking for smooth, intuitive experiences that are marked by privacy, security, and user control.Intelligent wearables comprise much of the hardware of this “ecosystem of you.” Consumers are interested in ecosystems instead of single devices, and they’re looking for agentic AI capabilities that understand and act on their behalf.Yet so much of the industry remains undefined. OEMs and technology makers have an enormous opportunity right now to innovate and iterate on the strong technological foundations that platform makers are building. And the roadmap for what consumers want is clear.All percentages, consumer behaviors, and attitudes stated in this report are based only on the responses of the individuals who participated in our survey.
